LH-REG-003.question: An insurer incorporated in Ohio has received a certificate of authority from Washington and sells policies there. In Washington, it is considered:
LH-REG-003.explanation: RCW 48.05.010 defines a foreign insurer as one formed under the laws of another U.S. state, and a certificate of authority from the commissioner (RCW 48.05.030) makes it authorized, or admitted. It would be non-admitted only without that certificate, and it is domestic only in Ohio.

LH-PROV-004.explanation: Washington requires a grace period of one month, but not less than 30 days, and the policy stays in force during it (RCW 48.23.030). Death on March 20 falls within it, so the insurer pays the face amount minus the overdue premium: $100,000 - $1,200 = $98,800.

LH-PROV-011.explanation: Washington lets an individual life policyowner return the policy within 10 days after receiving it for a full premium refund, and the policy is then void from the start (RCW 48.23.380). No premium is forfeited, and a refund paid more than 30 days after the return carries a 10 percent penalty.

LH-PROV-016.explanation: Washington's simultaneous death law (RCW 11.05A.030) treats a beneficiary who is not shown by clear and convincing evidence to have survived the insured by 120 hours as having died first. Proceeds therefore go as if the insured survived: to the contingent beneficiary or, if none, the insured's estate.

LH-HPRV-001.explanation: Washington's standard grace period provision (RCW 48.20.062) requires at least 10 days for monthly premiums, so coverage continues through June 11 and any unpaid premium can be deducted from a claim. The 7-day minimum applies only to weekly premiums, and 31 days applies to other modes.

excluded.LH-LIFE-001: Divorce and an ex-spouse owner-beneficiary: Washington's nonprobate asset revocation statute (RCW 11.07.010) makes the outcome turn on who made the designation, so the item is not used rather than risk a second defensible answer.
excluded.LH-PROV-005: Life reinstatement terms (three years in most policies) are not set by a Washington statute found in RCW 48.23; not asserted.
excluded.LH-HPRV-018: 75 percent group participation is an underwriting custom, not Washington law; left out to keep the form on the outline.
